text: A strange chill. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether it was the chill of the room. <break time="0.8s" /> Or of their own bodies. <break time="0.8s" /> Now began to creep. <break time="0.8s" /> Gradually over them all. <break time="0.8s" /> The doctor took up the rose of half a century. <break time="0.8s" /> And they saw with dismay. <break time="0.8s" /> That its fresh petals were already shriveling. <break time="0.8s" /> Until it became as dry and fragile. <break time="0.8s" /> As before. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking at one another. <break time="0.8s" /> They shuddered. <break time="0.8s" /> For they saw. <break time="0.8s" /> That the deep furrows of age were returning. <break time="0.8s" /> And that each of them. <break time="0.8s" /> Was once again an old, withered person. <break time="0.8s" /> Are we grown old again, so soon. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried they, dolefully. <break time="0.8s" /> And indeed the Water of Youth. <break time="0.8s" /> Possessed merely a virtue. <break time="0.8s" /> More transient than that of wine. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, friends, ye are old again. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Doctor Heidegger. <break time="0.8s" /> And, lo, the Water of Youth. <break time="0.8s" /> Is all lavished on the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> But I do not lament it. <break time="0.8s" /> For if the fountain gushed. <break time="0.8s" /> At my very doorstep. <break time="0.8s" /> I would not stoop. <break time="0.8s" /> To bathe my lips in it. <break time="0.8s" /> No, though its delirium were for years. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead of moments. <break time="0.8s" /> Such is the lesson. <break time="0.8s" /> Ye have taught me. <break time="0.8s" /> But the doctors four friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Had taught no such lesson. <break time="0.8s" /> To themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> They resolved forthwith. <break time="0.8s" /> To make a pilgrimage to Florida. <break time="0.8s" /> And there to drink. <break time="0.8s" /> At morning, noon, and night. <break time="0.8s" /> From the Fountain of Youth.
